about: Registry of page blocks for render.py. Pick a block by `purpose`/`use_when`, fill its fields in post.json. Text fields marked (md) take inline Markdown (**bold**, `code`, [link](url), *em*); fields marked (md-block) take full Markdown (paragraphs, lists, ### headings, tables, fences). pill = {"kind": ok|warn|bad|info|acc|mute, "text": "..."} with the fixed meanings in references/design-system.md. link = ["label", "#id or https://url"]. `nested` lists the fields each list item takes; render.py checks them too. Kinds and cols are checked against the fixed sets.

hero.purpose: Page opener: kicker, claim headline, lede, meta chips, up to 4 stat tiles.
hero.use_when: Always — set as post.json `hero`, not inside a section.

optional.kicker: what this is and for whom
optional.title: (md) *phrase* renders as the accent italic
optional.signal: false hides the drawn signal line

section.purpose: Numbered page section; becomes one TOC entry. Set as an item of post.json `sections` with its own `blocks`.
section.use_when: Always — every block lives in a section.

optional.intro: (md) one or two sentences under the heading
optional.toc_group: group heading shown above this entry in the TOC (e.g. Part 2 · ...)
optional.head: false hides the heading (checklist / start sections carry their own)

md.purpose: Prose: paragraphs, lists, quotes, ### / #### headings, tables, fenced code.
md.use_when: Running text. The default block; switch to a structured block when the content has a shape (steps, comparison, key-values).

callout.purpose: One highlighted point the reader must not miss.
callout.use_when: A key takeaway (key), a caution (warn) or a side note (note).

optional.title: short label
optional.text: (md-block) — leave out for a title-only label (e.g. 'Example — illustrative') above the block it introduces

table.purpose: Tabular facts; also capability matrices (✓ ~ ✗) and glossaries.

optional.head: [(md)]
optional.wide: true sets a min width and scrolls sideways on phones
optional.key: false stops bolding the first column (default true)
optional.sel: matrix column index to highlight (the recommended option)
optional.caption: (md) bold line above the table
optional.note: (md) caption line under the block: the takeaway
optional.ascii: plain-text twin shown in the Markdown tab instead of the table

cards.purpose: A grid of short cards: benefits, side-by-side comparison, facts, groups of items.
cards.use_when: 2–6 parallel items that each need a title and a short body.

optional.note: (md) caption line under the block: the takeaway
optional.ascii: plain-text twin shown in the Markdown tab instead of the default list

steps.purpose: An ordered flow or pipeline: numbered step cards that wrap on small screens.
steps.use_when: A sequence where order matters (request → response → handling), optionally looping.

optional.loop: (md) note shown as ↺ under the steps
optional.note: (md) caption line under the block: the takeaway
optional.ascii: plain-text twin shown in the Markdown tab instead of the default list

kv.purpose: A receipt-style sheet of key → value rows.
kv.use_when: Showing the fields of one object (a response header, a bill, a config).

optional.title: sheet label
optional.note: (md) caption line under the block: the takeaway
optional.ascii: plain-text twin shown in the Markdown tab instead of the default list

tags.purpose: A wrap of small labelled tiles, each coloured by meaning, with an optional legend.
tags.use_when: Enumerating values with a status (stop reasons, error codes, states).

optional.note: (md) caption line under the block: the takeaway
optional.ascii: plain-text twin shown in the Markdown tab instead of the default list

figure.purpose: A hand-drawn inline SVG diagram with a caption and optional ASCII twin for the Markdown tab.
figure.use_when: A picture shows the mechanism better than words. Use theme classes only (references/design-system.md).

optional.file: path to an .svg fragment, relative to post.json (preferred for anything long)
optional.caption: (md) the conclusion
optional.ascii: plain-text version: shown in the Markdown tab and under the figure
optional.fit: true lets a small diagram shrink on phones instead of scrolling

image.purpose: An image file (svg, png, webp, jpg, gif) embedded into the page as a data URI, with an optional dark-theme variant. Width and height are read from the file (svg viewBox, png, gif) so the layout doesn't shift while it loads.
image.use_when: A diagram or picture already exists as a file (e.g. a rendered Mermaid chart, a screenshot) and redrawing it with theme classes isn't worth it. Prefer `figure` for new diagrams.

optional.file: path relative to post.json; embedded, so the page stays one file
optional.file_dark: variant shown in dark theme (light one hides)
optional.alt: (md) what the image shows, for screen readers and the Markdown tab
optional.caption: (md) the conclusion
optional.ascii: text twin for the Markdown tab and the fold-out under the image (e.g. the Mermaid source)
optional.ascii_lang: fence language for the twin in Markdown (default text; e.g. mermaid)
optional.fit: true lets the image shrink on phones instead of scrolling sideways

code.use_when: Code, commands, schemas, config the reader may copy.

video.purpose: An embedded YouTube video in a 16:9 frame, with a Watch-on-YouTube link under it.
video.use_when: The post is notes on, or refers to, a talk or demo video.

optional.youtube: the 11-character video id (the part after watch?v=)
optional.title: (md) video title — iframe title and the Markdown link text
optional.caption: (md) line shown before the link

checklist.purpose: Interactive checklist; ticks persist in the browser. One per page.
checklist.use_when: The reader should work through steps (review steps, rollout checks, what-to-do lists).

start.purpose: 'Start here' box: a reading route plus 1–3 columns of what to change / answer / skim.
start.use_when: Long pages where readers need a fast path.

optional.route_label: text before the route, e.g. 10-minute path
optional.columns: [[{title, items: [{text (md), refs: [link]?}]?, text (md)?}]] — each column is a list of groups

findings.purpose: Filterable finding cards (What · Example · Value · Fix). One per page.

optional.items: [{id, title (md), pill?, tags: [tag], fields: [[label, text (md-block), 'ex'|'val'?]], svg?}]

fcards.purpose: Labelled cards with an ID, a status pill and label → text rows (decisions, rules, cases, examples).
fcards.use_when: Items that each carry an ID and the same set of fields, without filtering.

explain.purpose: ID'd cards with always-visible label → text rows and a collapsible detail (rows plus an optional diagram) the reader opens on demand.
explain.use_when: Principles, rules or symptoms where the short form fits on the card and a worked case explains it: the case goes in `detail`.

optional.items: [{id, title (md), rows: [[label, text (md-block), 'ex'|'val'?]], detail: same shape as rows?, summary (md)? (overrides the block's), fig: {file | svg, caption (md), ascii?}?, pill?, meta (md)?}]
optional.note: (md) caption line under the block: the takeaway

options.purpose: Design option cards: goal, how, strong, weak, table sketches; one marked chosen.

optional.items: [{title (md), why (md)?, chosen?, tag: pill?, intent: [[label, text (md)]]?, tables: [{name, note?, cols: ['col' | ['col', 'key'|'warn'|'bad']]}]?, note (md)?}]

qgroups.purpose: Business questions grouped by job, each with an ID and example.
qgroups.use_when: Listing the questions a design must answer.

questions.purpose: Open questions as a two-column grid.

requirements.purpose: Numbered requirement list with mono counters.

status.purpose: Status cards with a coloured left bar.
status.use_when: Per-item readiness or ownership (moments, layers, owners).

raw.purpose: Escape hatch: hand-written HTML using the shell's classes.
raw.use_when: Nothing above fits. Prefer adding a new block to the registry when the shape will recur.

optional.md: what the Markdown tab shows instead

footer.purpose: Closing line. Set as post.json `footer` (a string).
